articleBody:
Before you sign a contract for garage drywall installation, verify that the scope covers structural safety, moisture prevention, and proper separation assemblies. Use this practical checklist to review your garage setup before work starts.

- [ ] A tape measure reading of ceiling height and joist spacing — Joist spacing dictates whether specific drywall thicknesses or framing reinforcements are needed to avoid sagging.
- [ ] Identification of all walls sharing space with the house interior — Walls adjacent to living areas require specific separation assemblies and fire-rated gypsum board.
- [ ] Verification of occupied rooms situated directly above the garage ceiling — Living spaces above ceilings often mandate 5/8-inch Type X drywall rather than standard half-inch board.
- [ ] A moisture inspection of all perimeter framing and sill plates — Enclosing damp or damaged lumber behind fresh drywall leads to hidden decay and mold growth.
- [ ] Documentation of all wiring, gas lines, and plumbing penetrations — Every utility penetration through a separation wall must be sealed with approved firestopping compounds.
- [ ] A plan for lifting drywall off the concrete garage floor slab — Bottom panels must remain elevated slightly above concrete to prevent moisture absorption from winter vehicles.
- [ ] Confirmation of local building permit and inspection expectations — Different municipalities around Denver enforce specific amendments regarding garage-to-house separation assemblies.

How to use this checklist
Walk your garage with this list before requesting quotes. Discuss these items with HH Remodeling LLC to ensure your installation meets your household needs. Call 303-505-0866 to schedule an on-site consultation.
